questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

A utility maximising consumer spends the whole of his disposable income of $40 on food and clothing. The table shows the price of food, the quantity purchased by the consumer, and the marginal utility he derives from food consumption. food price per unit $5 quantity demanded 5 marginal utility (units) 10 His marginal utility from clothing is 2 units. What is the price of clothing per unit and the quantity purchased by the consumer? clothing price quantity ($) (units)
The curve JK in the diagram is a consumer’s initial budget line. G J good Y O H K good X Which combination could cause the budget line to shift to GH? consumer’s price of money income good Y

options.A: decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: A firm employs two factors, X and Y, to produce a good which is sold for $4. The table shows its factor productivities and factor prices. marginal physical factor price factor product ($) X 3 15 Y 5 12 What should the firm do?

options.A: employ less of both X and Y
options.B: employ more of X and less of Y
options.C: employ more of Y and less of X
options.D: employ more of both X and Y

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the total product of labour curve for a firm whose only variable factor input is labour. TPL total product of labour O number employed What explains the shape of the curve?

options.A: diminishing marginal disutility of work
options.B: increasing marginal disutility of work
options.C: technical diseconomies of scale
options.D: the law of variable proportions

questions.questionText: A worker responds to an increase in his hourly wage rate by reducing the number of hours he works per week. What would explain this?

options.A: The income effect of the wage rate increase outweighs the substitution effect.
options.B: The substitution effect of the wage rate increase outweighs the income effect.
options.C: The worker’s supply of labour is wage elastic.
options.D: The worker’s supply of labour is wage inelastic.

questions.questionText: There is an increase in the supply of female labour. What will be the likely effect on male and female wages? male wages female wages

options.A: decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: Samsung Electronics, which began as a semiconductor firm making simple memory chips, has used continuous research and investment to emerge as an industry leader. In addition, it has applied its strength in semiconductors to other markets including televisions and mobile phones. What has taken place?

options.A: external growth and diversification
options.B: external growth and sales revenue maximisation
options.C: internal growth and diversification
options.D: internal growth and sales revenue maximisation

questions.questionText: The price elasticity of demand for a firm’s product is zero. What will be the effect on the firm’s revenue if it reduces its price by 5%?

options.A: Its revenue will fall to zero.
options.B: Its revenue will be unchanged.
options.C: Its revenue will decrease by 5%.
options.D: Its revenue will increase by 5%.

questions.questionText: What explains why both large and small firms are often found within the same industry?

options.A: All firms in the industry produce identical products.
options.B: Firms that assemble the final product buy components from specialist firms within the industry.
options.C: Production within the industry is subject to diseconomies of scale.
options.D: There are significant barriers to the entry of new firms into the industry.

questions.questionText: Which condition must apply before a market can be regarded as perfectly contestable?

options.A: All firms in the industry produce an identical product.
options.B: All firms in the industry are price-takers.
options.C: There are a large number of firms in the industry.
options.D: There are zero costs of entry to, and exit from, the industry.

questions.questionText: The table shows the total revenue and marginal cost of a firm at different levels of production. production total marginal (tonnes) revenue ($) cost ($)
An industry moves from monopolistic competition to oligopoly. How will this affect barriers to entry and the degree of interdependence between firms? interdependence barriers to entry between firms

options.A: strengthen strengthen
options.B: strengthen weaken
options.C: weaken strengthen
options.D: weaken weaken

questions.questionText: In the diagram, D is a country’s demand curve for an imported good. The world price of the good is OP . W P c price x y P w z D O quantity Which area measures the deadweight loss to the country of imposing an import tariff equal to P P on the good? W C

options.A: x B y C z D x + y

questions.questionText: A government decides to privatise a state monopoly. What should the government do to try to ensure that this will result in an improvement in efficiency?

options.A: allocate vouchers to all citizens entitling them to a share in the ownership of the monopoly
options.B: encourage competition
options.C: impose a maximum profit margin
options.D: privatise the monopoly as a going concern

questions.questionText: What might make Gross National Product (GNP) per capita a misleading indicator when comparing living standards in different countries?

options.A: differences between market exchange rates and purchasing power parity exchange rates
options.B: differences in capital investment as a proportion of GNP
options.C: differences in exports and imports as a proportion of GNP
options.D: differences in net property income from abroad

questions.questionText: Due to a cyclical downturn, a government is experiencing a budget deficit. If the government wishes to stimulate aggregate demand, which policy would be most effective?

options.A: financing the deficit by borrowing from the Central Bank
options.B: financing the deficit by selling bonds to individuals
options.C: financing the deficit by selling state assets to private firms
options.D: increasing tax rates to eliminate the deficit

questions.questionText: Which represents a leakage from a country’s circular flow of income?

options.A: a government budget deficit
options.B: bank loans to private companies
options.C: the purchase of foreign assets by the country’s households
options.D: unemployment benefits

questions.questionText: Which statement would be consistent with a monetarist view of the workings of the macroeconomy?

options.A: The demand for money function can shift in an unpredictable way.
options.B: The velocity of circulation of money is unstable over time.
options.C: Interest rates have little effect on aggregate money expenditure.
options.D: A sustained inflation is always associated with an increasing money supply.

questions.questionText: In a closed economy with no government, the equilibrium level of income is $25 million, the full employment level of income is $30 million and there is a deflationary gap of $1 million. What can be deduced from this information?

options.A: The level of investment is $5 million.
options.B: The marginal propensity to consume is 4 .
options.C: The marginal propensity to consume is 5 .
options.D: The value of the investment multiplier is 1.5.

questions.questionText: In the diagram, C shows the initial relationship between consumption and national income. C C consumption O national income What could cause the consumption function to shift to C ?

options.A: an increase in the rate of unemployment benefits
options.B: an increase in the standard rate of income tax
options.C: an increase in exports
options.D: an increase in investment

questions.questionText: Other things being equal, the money supply in an open economy will increase if

options.A: domestic banks increase their lending to foreign borrowers.
options.B: the central bank buys foreign currency in the foreign exchange market.
options.C: the government sells bonds to domestic residents.
options.D: there is an increase in the volume of imports to the economy.

questions.questionText: According to Keynesian theory, in which circumstance would there always be an increase in the demand for money? real income price level interest rates

options.A: increase decrease increase
options.B: constant constant increase
options.C: increase increase decrease
options.D: constant decrease decrease

questions.questionText: Which change would best indicate that a country has experienced economic development?

options.A: an appreciation in the country’s currency
options.B: an improvement in the average citizen‘s quality of life
options.C: an improvement in the country’s trade balance
options.D: an increase in the country’s real GDP

questions.questionText: The table shows the figures for consumption, capital formation and depreciation in four economies, all measured in US $. Assuming that the state of technology remains unchanged, which economy is most likely to experience economic growth? consumption capital formation depreciation ($ m) ($ m) ($ m)
How will outward migration from a developing economy affect its balance of payments?

options.A: It may improve its balance of payments by increasing its export capacity.
options.B: It may improve its balance of payments by increasing inflows of current transfers.
options.C: It may worsen its balance of payments by causing its currency to depreciate.
options.D: It may worsen its balance of payments by increasing consumer expenditure on imported goods.

questions.questionText: A government’s priority is to reduce the natural rate of unemployment (NAIRU). Which policy would be most likely to help it achieve this objective?

options.A: an increase in interest rates
options.B: an increase in rates of unemployment benefit
options.C: the introduction of minimum wage rates
options.D: the introduction of subsidised travel for unemployed workers to search for jobs

questions.questionText: Other things being equal, what is likely to result from a reduction in interest rates in a country?

options.A: an appreciation of the country’s currency
options.B: a decrease in consumption
options.C: a decrease in investment
options.D: an outflow of short-term capital

questions.questionText: The European Union imposes a quota on the volume of garments imported from China. What is likely to be a consequence?

options.A: an increase in the prices received by Chinese textile firms
options.B: a reduction in the prices paid by EU consumers
options.C: a switch to producing lower-value garments by Chinese textile firms
options.D: a reduction in the volume of garments exported from China to non-EU markets

questions.questionText: A government responds to cyclical fluctuations in output by keeping tax rates and benefit rates unchanged. What is the government seeking to achieve by adopting this fiscal policy?

options.A: to allow automatic stabilisers to work
options.B: to keep output at the full employment level
options.C: to maintain a constant balanced budget
options.D: to ensure that its budget is in surplus over the trade cycle reasonable effort has been made by the publisher (UCLES) to trace copyright holders, but if any items requiring clearance have unwittingly been included, the publisher will be pleased to make amends at the earliest possible opportunity.
